findings.title: Concurrent same-author tool errors merge thought id
findings.problem: _active_error_streak in AgentStreamingCallback.on_tool_error is keyed only by author, not by run_id or tool-call. When parallel tool calling is enabled (a live, configurable option, e.g. smart_react_agent.py's parallel_tool_calls) and two tool calls from the same author fail concurrently rather than as sequential retries, the second error's thought.id is aliased onto the first error's already-existing streak id.
findings.impact: The UI shows one tool's error message under the wrong tool's visible thought, hiding which of the two concurrently-failing tools actually produced which error.
findings.recommendation: Scope the streak key by (author, originating run_id/tool_call chain) or only alias thought.id when the new error's call genuinely chains from the same prior tool call (sequential retry), not merely 'same author'.

findings.title: Consecutive-error cap not scoped per subagent
findings.problem: self._consecutive_tool_error_count is a single scalar on the LangGraphAgent instance whose own _stream_graph loop is actually executing. In supervisor/multi-agent mode, AssistantFactory.build() constructs a separate LangGraphAgent per subagent only to extract its compiled .agent_executor; that per-subagent instance's own _on_tool_error is never invoked again at runtime. All tool-error events, including those from nested subagent subgraphs (tagged only by an author string), are parsed and dispatched through the one top-level instance's _stream_graph/_event_adapter loop and its single shared counter.
findings.impact: AC6 requires each subagent (incl. parallel Send branches) to track its own independent error streak. Instead, a tool success from any one subagent resets the shared counter (letting a genuinely broken subagent dodge the cap), and unrelated single errors interleaved across different subagents accumulate on the shared counter and can abort the entire multi-agent run even though no individual subagent hit N consecutive errors.
findings.recommendation: Key the counter by author (a dict, mirroring _active_error_streak in AgentStreamingCallback), incrementing/resetting per author rather than on the single instance-wide scalar.

findings.title: Tool-error cap skips thought finalization
findings.problem: _on_tool_error raises MaxConsecutiveToolErrorsExceededException as soon as the cap is reached, before ever reaching the existing call to self._callback_bridge.on_tool_error(output, run_id=run_id, author=author) a few lines below. That callback is the only code path that sets the triggering tool's thought in_progress=False/error=True and sends it to the client (AgentStreamingCallback.on_tool_error).
findings.impact: The tool call that triggers the fatal abort has its Thought left permanently 'in progress' in the UI, reproducing the exact 'thought remains in progress' defect this ticket was opened to fix, specifically for the one call that ends the run.
findings.recommendation: Call self._callback_bridge.on_tool_error(output, run_id=run_id, author=author) (or an equivalent finalize-thought step) before or regardless of raising MaxConsecutiveToolErrorsExceededException, so the triggering tool's thought is always finalized.
